title.zh: 卷六 梁本紀上第六 武帝上
title.raw: 卷六 梁本紀上第六 武帝上 Volume 6 :Liang Annals 1: Emperor Wu 1

sentences.zh: 梁本紀上第六

translations.literal: Liang Annals 1, Part Six
translations.idiomatic: Liang Annals 1, Part Six

sentences.zh: 梁高祖武皇帝諱衍，字叔達，小字練兒，南蘭陵中都里人，姓蕭氏，與齊同承淮陰令整。

translations.literal: The Liang High Ancestor Emperor Wu, taboo name Yan, style name Shuda, childhood name Lian'er, was a native of Zhongdu Village in Nan Luling, surname Xiao, sharing descent from Huaiyin Magistrate Zheng with the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang High Ancestor Emperor Wu — taboo name Yan, style name Shuda, childhood name Lian'er — came from Zhongdu Village in Nan Luling. The Xiao clan traced its line, like the Qi, from Huaiyin Magistrate Zheng.

sentences.zh: 整生皇高祖轄，位濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Zheng begat the Imperial High Ancestor Xia, who held the post of Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng fathered the Imperial High Ancestor Xia, who served as Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 轄生皇曾祖副子，位州治中從事。

translations.literal: Xia begat the Imperial Great-Grandfather Fuzi, who held the post of Assistant Administrator of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Xia fathered the Imperial Great-Grandfather Fuzi, who served as Assistant Administrator of the province.

sentences.zh: 副子生皇祖道賜，位南台治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Fuzi begat the Imperial Grandfather Daoci, who held the post of Supervising Censor of the Southern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzi fathered the Imperial Grandfather Daoci, who served as Supervising Censor of the Southern Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 道賜生皇考，諱順之，字文緯，于齊高帝為始族弟。

translations.literal: Daoci begat the Imperial Father, taboo name Shunzhi, style name Wenwei, who to Emperor Gao of Qi was a first cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoci fathered the Imperial Father, whose taboo name was Shunzhi and style name Wenwei — a first cousin once removed of Emperor Gao of Qi.

sentences.zh: 皇考外甚清和，而內懷英氣，與齊高少而款狎。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father outwardly was very mild and harmonious, yet inwardly harbored heroic spirit; with Emperor Gao of Qi he was intimate from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the Imperial Father was gentle and even-tempered; inwardly he carried a warrior's fire. From boyhood he and Emperor Gao of Qi were close companions.

sentences.zh: 嘗共登金牛山，路側有枯骨縱橫，齊高謂皇考曰：「周文王以來幾年，當復有掩此枯骨者乎？

translations.literal: Once they climbed Mount Jinniu together; by the roadside bleached bones lay scattered. Emperor Gao said to the Imperial Father, "Since King Wen of Zhou, how many years have passed — will there again be one who covers these dry bones?"
translations.idiomatic: Once they climbed Mount Jinniu together. Bleached bones lay scattered by the road. Emperor Gao turned to the Imperial Father and asked, "Since King Wen of Zhou — how many years have passed? Will anyone again come to bury these dry bones?"

sentences.zh: 」言之懍然動色。

translations.literal: " As he spoke, his expression changed with solemn dread.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, his face darkened with solemn dread.

sentences.zh: 皇考由此知齊高有大志，常相隨逐。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father thereby knew Emperor Gao had great ambition, and constantly followed in his train.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Imperial Father knew that Emperor Gao nursed great ambition, and he kept close at his side thereafter.

sentences.zh: 齊高每外討，皇考常為軍副。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Gao campaigned abroad, the Imperial Father regularly served as deputy commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gao marched abroad, the Imperial Father usually served as his army's second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 及北討，薛索兒夜遣人入營，提刀徑至齊高眠床，皇考手刃之。

translations.literal: During a northern campaign, Xue Suo'er by night sent a man into the camp who, knife in hand, went straight to Emperor Gao's sleeping couch; the Imperial Father cut him down with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: On a northern campaign, Xue Suo'er sent a man by night into the camp. Knife in hand, the assassin went straight to Emperor Gao's bed — and the Imperial Father struck him down himself.

sentences.zh: 頻為齊高鎮軍司馬、長史。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he served Emperor Gao as Army Marshal and Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held the posts of Army Marshal and Chief Administrator under Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 時宋帝昏虐，齊高謀出外，皇考以為一旦奔亡，則危幾不測，不如因人之欲，行伊、霍之事，齊高深然之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Song was benighted and cruel; Emperor Gao plotted to go abroad. The Imperial Father thought that if they fled in a single night, peril would be incalculable — better to act on the people's desire and do as Yi Yin and Huo Guang had done. Emperor Gao deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Song was benighted and cruel, and Emperor Gao plotted flight abroad. The Imperial Father argued that a sudden escape would invite incalculable peril — better to act on public will and do as Yi Yin and Huo Guang had done. Emperor Gao agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 曆黃門郎，安西長史，吳郡內史，所經皆著名。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Chief Administrator of the Anxi Command, Interior Minister of Wu Commandery — wherever he served he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Chief Administrator of the Anxi Command, and Interior Minister of Wu Commandery — and wherever he went, his name carried weight.

sentences.zh: 吳郡張緒常稱：「文武兼資，有德有行，吾敬蕭順之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu of Wu Commandery often said, "Both civil and military in talent, with virtue and conduct — I revere Xiao Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu of Wu Commandery often said, "Civil and martial both — with virtue and conduct to match. I revere Xiao Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 」袁粲之據石頭，黃回與之通謀，皇考聞難作，率家兵據朱雀橋，回覘人還告曰：「朱雀橋南一長者，英威毅然，坐胡床南向。

translations.literal: " When Yuan Can held Shitou, Huang Hui conspired with him; hearing trouble had broken out, the Imperial Father led household troops to hold Zhuque Bridge. Hui sent a scout back to report, "South of Zhuque Bridge there is a tall elder, stern and resolute in bearing, seated on a folding chair facing south.
translations.idiomatic: "When Yuan Can held Shitou and Huang Hui plotted with him, the Imperial Father heard trouble had erupted and led household troops to seize Zhuque Bridge. Hui's scout returned to report: "South of Zhuque Bridge sits a tall elder — stern, resolute — on a folding chair facing south.

sentences.zh: 」回曰：「蕭順之也。

translations.literal: " Hui said, "That is Xiao Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: "Hui said, "That is Xiao Shunzhi."

sentences.zh: 」遂不敢出。

translations.literal: " He then dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He then dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 時微皇考，石頭幾不據矣。

translations.literal: At that time, but for the Imperial Father, Shitou would nearly not have been held.
translations.idiomatic: But for the Imperial Father, Shitou would scarcely have held.

sentences.zh: 及齊高創造皇業，推鋒決勝，莫不垂拱仰成焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao founded the imperial enterprise, in thrusting forward to decide victory none failed to defer to his accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao founded the dynasty, every thrust toward victory owed something to the Imperial Father's handiwork.

sentences.zh: 齊建元末，齊高從容謂皇考曰：「當令阿玉解揚州相授。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Jianyuan era, Emperor Gao said at ease to the Imperial Father, "I shall have A-yu relinquish Yang Province and hand it over to you.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jianyuan era, Emperor Gao said casually to the Imperial Father, "I mean to have A-yu yield Yang Province and transfer it to you.

sentences.zh: 」玉，豫章王嶷小名也。

translations.literal: " Yu was the childhood name of Prince of Yuzhang, Niao.
translations.idiomatic: "Yu was the childhood name of Prince of Yuzhang, Niao.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝在東宮，皇考嘗問訊，及退，齊武指皇考謂嶷曰：「非此翁，吾徒無以致今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi was in the Eastern Palace; the Imperial Father once came to pay respects, and after he withdrew, Emperor Wu pointed to the Imperial Father and said to Niao, "But for this old man, we would never have reached today.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi was then in the Eastern Palace. After the Imperial Father paid a visit and withdrew, Emperor Wu pointed him out to Niao and said, "Without this old man, we would never have reached today.

sentences.zh: 」及即位，深相忌憚，故不居台輔。

translations.literal: " When he took the throne, he deeply envied and feared him, and therefore did not appoint him to the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: "When he took the throne, he deeply envied and feared the Imperial Father, and so never gave him a seat among the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 以參豫佐命，封臨湘縣侯。

translations.literal: For sharing in the founding merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For sharing in the founding merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中，衛尉，太子詹事，領軍將軍，丹陽尹，贈鎮北將軍，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, General Who Leads the Army, Governor of Danyang; posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the North, with posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and General Who Leads the Army, and served as Governor of Danyang. Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the North, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝以宋孝武大明八年歲次甲辰生於秣陵縣同夏裏三橋宅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was born in the eighth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, year jiachen, at the Three-Bridge residence in Tongxia Village, Moling County.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was born in the eighth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song — the year jiachen — at the Three-Bridge residence in Tongxia Village, Moling County.

sentences.zh: 初，皇妣張氏嘗夢抱日，已而有娠，遂產帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Imperial Mother née Zhang once dreamed she embraced the sun; afterward she conceived, and thus bore the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Imperial Mother, née Zhang, had dreamed she held the sun in her arms; soon after she conceived and bore the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝生而有異光，狀貌殊特，日角龍顏，重岳虎顧，舌文八字，項有浮光，身映日無影，兩骻駢骨，項上隆起，有文在右手曰：「武」。

translations.literal: At birth the Emperor had unusual radiance; his form was extraordinary — sun-angled brow, dragon countenance, heavy mountain peaks, tiger's backward glance, eight-character pattern on the tongue, floating light on the nape, body casting no shadow in sunlight, paired shin-bones, a raised ridge on the neck, and on the right hand the character "Wu."
translations.idiomatic: At birth he shone with unusual light. His form was extraordinary: sun-angled brow, dragon countenance, heavy mountain peaks, a tiger's backward glance, an eight-character pattern on the tongue, floating light on the nape, a body that cast no shadow in sunlight, paired shin-bones, a raised ridge on the neck, and on his right hand the character Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝為兒時，能蹈空而行。

translations.literal: As a child the Emperor could tread empty air and walk.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy the Emperor could tread empty air and walk.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學多通，好籌略，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: When grown, he was broadly learned and widely versed, fond of strategy, and possessed both civil and martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he was broadly learned, fond of strategy, and possessed both civil and martial talent.

sentences.zh: 所居室中，常若雲氣，人或遇者，體輒肅然。

translations.literal: In the rooms where he dwelt, there was often as if cloud-vapor; those who encountered it would at once feel solemn awe.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-vapor seemed often to fill the rooms where he dwelt; those who encountered it felt an involuntary solemn awe.

sentences.zh: 初為衛軍王儉東合祭酒，儉一見深相器異，請為戶曹屬。

translations.literal: At first he was Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under Wang Jian, General of the Guard; Jian, on first meeting, deeply valued and marked him as extraordinary, and requested him as a member of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under Wang Jian, General of the Guard. On first meeting, Jian marked him as extraordinary and requested him for the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 謂廬江何憲曰：「此蕭郎三十內當作侍中，出此則貴不可言。

translations.literal: He said to He Xian of Lujiang, "This Master Xiao within thirty years will become Attendant-in-Ordinary; beyond that, his nobility cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: He told He Xian of Lujiang, "This Master Xiao will be Attendant-in-Ordinary within thirty years — and beyond that, his eminence cannot be put into words.

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，帝與沈約、謝朓、王融、蕭琛、范雲、任昉、陸倕等並遊焉，號曰：「八友」。

translations.literal: " When Prince of Jingling Ziliang opened the Western Lodge and gathered men of letters, the Emperor joined Shen Yue, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, Lu Chui, and others in fellowship there; they were called the "Eight Friends."
translations.idiomatic: "When Prince of Jingling Ziliang opened the Western Lodge and gathered men of letters, the Emperor joined Shen Yue, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, Lu Chui, and others there — they were called the Eight Friends.

sentences.zh: 融俊爽，識鑒過人，尤敬異帝，每謂所親曰：「宰製天下，必在此人。

translations.literal: Rong was handsome and bright, with insight surpassing others; he especially revered and marked the Emperor as extraordinary, and often said to those close to him, "He who will rule the realm must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was handsome and bright, with insight surpassing others. He especially revered the Emperor and often told those close to him, "He who will rule the realm must be this man.

sentences.zh: 」累遷隨王鎮西諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " He was repeatedly promoted to Adviser to the General Who Guards the West under the Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: "He rose repeatedly to Adviser to the General Who Guards the West under the Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 行經牛渚，逢風，入泊龍瀆，有一老人謂帝曰：「君龍行虎步，相不可言，天下方亂，安之者其在君乎？

translations.literal: Passing by Niuzhu, he met wind and entered Longdu to moor; an old man said to the Emperor, "Your dragon stride and tiger step — your physiognomy cannot be told. The realm is about to fall into disorder; will the one who settles it be you?
translations.idiomatic: Passing Niuzhu, he met wind and moored at Longdu. An old man said to the Emperor, "Your dragon stride and tiger step — such a countenance cannot be spoken of. The realm is falling into disorder; will you be the one to settle it?

sentences.zh: 」問其名氏，忽然不見。

translations.literal: " Asked his surname, he suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his name, the old man suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 尋以皇考艱去職，歸建鄴。

translations.literal: Soon after, on the Imperial Father's bereavement he left office and returned to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, on the Imperial Father's death he left office and returned to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 及齊武帝不豫，竟陵王子良以帝及兄懿、王融、劉繪、王思遠、顧暠之、範雲等為帳內軍主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Qi fell ill, Prince of Jingling Ziliang made the Emperor, his elder brother Yi, Wang Rong, Liu Hui, Wang Siyuan, Gu Tan, Fan Yun, and others commanders within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Qi fell ill, Prince of Jingling Ziliang made the Emperor, his elder brother Yi, Wang Rong, Liu Hui, Wang Siyuan, Gu Tan, Fan Yun, and others commanders within the tent.

sentences.zh: 融欲因帝晏駕立子良，帝曰：「夫立非常之事，必待非常之人，融才非負圖，視其敗也。

translations.literal: Rong wished to use the Emperor's death to install Ziliang; the Emperor said, "To establish an extraordinary affair one must await an extraordinary man — Rong's talent is not equal to bearing the realm; watch him fail.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to use the Emperor's death to install Ziliang. The Emperor said, "Extraordinary deeds require extraordinary men — Rong's talent is not equal to bearing the realm. Watch him fail.

sentences.zh: 」範雲曰：「憂國家者，惟有王中書。

translations.literal: " Fan Yun said, "He who worries for the state — there is only Wang Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: "Fan Yun said, "The one who worries for the state is Wang Zhongshu alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「憂國欲為周、召？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Do you wish to be Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao?
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor said, "Do you mean to be Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao?

sentences.zh: 欲為豎、刁邪？

translations.literal: Or do you wish to be Shu and Diao?
translations.idiomatic: Or do you mean to be Shu and Diao?

sentences.zh: 」懿曰：「直哉史魚，何其木強也！」

translations.literal: " Yi said, "How straight was Master Shi Yu — how obstinately wooden!"
translations.idiomatic: "Yi said, "How straight was Master Shi Yu — how obstinately wooden!"

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏將王肅、劉昶攻司州刺史蕭誕甚急，齊明遣左衛將軍王廣之赴救，帝為偏帥隸廣之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang pressed Governor of Si Province Xiao Dan very hard; Emperor Ming of Qi sent Left Guard General Wang Guangzhi to the rescue, and the Emperor served as a subordinate commander under Guangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang pressed Governor of Si Province Xiao Dan hard. Emperor Ming of Qi sent Left Guard General Wang Guangzhi to the rescue; the Emperor served as a subordinate commander under Guangzhi.

sentences.zh: 行次熨斗洲，有人長八尺餘，容貌衣冠皓然皆白，緣江呼曰：「蕭王大貴。

translations.literal: Stopping at Yandou Isle, there was a man over eight chi tall, face and garb all white, who along the river called out, "Great nobility to Lord Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: At Yandou Isle a man over eight chi tall, face and garb all white, called along the river, "Great nobility to Lord Xiao."

sentences.zh: 」帝既屢有征祥，心益自負。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having repeatedly had auspicious signs, grew ever more self-confident.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly received auspicious signs, the Emperor grew ever more self-confident.

sentences.zh: 時去誕百里，眾軍以魏軍盛，莫敢前。

translations.literal: At that time they were a hundred li from Dan; the armies, seeing the Wei forces strong, dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They were then a hundred li from Dan; seeing the Wei forces strong, the armies dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大振威略，謂諸將曰：「今屯下梁之城，塞鑿峴之險，守雉腳之路，據賢首之山，以通西關，以臨賊壘，三方掎角，出其不備，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished greatly to display martial strategy and said to the generals, "Now encamp at Xiabliang City, block the peril of Zuoxian, hold the road at Zhijiao, occupy Xianshou Mountain, open the Western Pass, and overlook the enemy camp — a three-sided pincer, striking where they do not expect: the bandits will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to display martial strategy and told the generals, "Encamp at Xiabliang City, block Zuoxian's peril, hold the road at Zhijiao, occupy Xianshou Mountain, open the Western Pass, and overlook the enemy camp — a three-sided pincer striking where they do not expect. The bandits will surely break.

sentences.zh: 」廣之等不從。

translations.literal: " Guangzhi and the others did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi and the others would not follow.

sentences.zh: 後遣徐玄慶進據賢首山，魏絕其糧道，眾懼，莫敢援之，惟帝獨奮請先進。

translations.literal: Later they sent Xu Xuanqing forward to hold Xianshou Mountain; the Wei cut his supply route. The troops feared and dared not aid him — only the Emperor alone urged advance and requested to go first.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Xuanqing was sent forward to hold Xianshou Mountain; the Wei cut his supply route. The troops feared and dared not aid him — only the Emperor urged advance and asked to go first.

sentences.zh: 於是廣之益帝精甲，銜枚夜前。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangzhi gave the Emperor picked armor; gagged, they advanced by night.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi then gave the Emperor picked armor; gagged, they advanced by night.

sentences.zh: 失道，望見如持兩炬者，隨之果得道，徑上賢首山，廣之軍因得前。

translations.literal: They lost the way; seeing what seemed two torches held, they followed and indeed found the road, going straight up Xianshou Mountain, and Guangzhi's army was thus able to advance.
translations.idiomatic: They lost the way; seeing what seemed two torches held, they followed and found the road, going straight up Xianshou Mountain — and Guangzhi's army was able to advance.

sentences.zh: 魏軍來脅，帝堅壁不進。

translations.literal: The Wei army came to press them; the Emperor held the walls and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army came to press them; the Emperor held the walls and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 時王肅自攻城，一鼓而退，劉昶有疑心，帝因與書，間成其隙。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Su himself attacked the city; one drum-stroke and he withdrew. Liu Chang had suspicions; the Emperor therefore wrote him letters and sowed discord between them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su himself attacked the city; one drum-stroke and he withdrew. Liu Chang grew suspicious; the Emperor wrote him letters and sowed discord between them.

sentences.zh: 一旦，有風從西北起，陣雲隨之來，當肅營，尋而風回雲轉，還向西北，帝曰：「此所謂歸氣，魏師遁矣。

translations.literal: One day wind rose from the northwest and battle-clouds followed, coming over Su's camp; soon the wind turned and clouds shifted back toward the northwest. The Emperor said, "This is what is called returning breath — the Wei army will flee.
translations.idiomatic: One day wind rose from the northwest and battle-clouds followed over Su's camp; soon wind and clouds shifted back northwest. The Emperor said, "This is returning breath — the Wei army will flee.

sentences.zh: 」令軍中曰：「望麾而進，聽鼓而動。

translations.literal: " He ordered the army, "Advance at the sight of the banner; move at the hearing of the drum.
translations.idiomatic: "He ordered the army, "Advance at the sight of the banner; move at the hearing of the drum.

sentences.zh: 」肅乃傾壁十萬，陣于水北，帝揚麾鼓噪，響振山谷，敢死之士，執短兵先登，長戟翼之。

translations.literal: " Su then deployed his full force of a hundred thousand, arrayed north of the water. The Emperor raised his banner and drummed with a clamor that shook valleys; dare-to-die men with short weapons climbed first, long halberds flanking them.
translations.idiomatic: Su deployed his full force of a hundred thousand north of the water. The Emperor raised his banner and drummed; the clamor shook the valleys. Dare-to-die men with short weapons climbed first, long halberds flanking them.

sentences.zh: 城中見援至，因出軍攻魏柵，魏軍表裏受敵，因大崩。

translations.literal: Seeing relief had arrived, the city sortied to attack the Wei palisade; the Wei army was attacked inside and out and collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing relief had arrived, the city sortied against the Wei palisade; attacked inside and out, the Wei army collapsed in great rout.

sentences.zh: 肅、昶單騎走，斬獲千計，流血絳野。

translations.literal: Su and Chang fled alone on horseback; the slain and captured numbered in the thousands, blood reddening the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Chang fled alone on horseback; slain and captured numbered in the thousands, blood reddening the wild.

sentences.zh: 得肅、昶巾箱中魏帝敕曰：「聞蕭衍善用兵，勿與爭鋒，待吾至；

translations.literal: From Su's and Chang's boxes they obtained an edict of the Wei Emperor saying, "I hear Xiao Yan is skilled in using troops — do not contend with him in the field; wait until I arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From Su's and Chang's boxes they found an edict of the Wei Emperor: "I hear Xiao Yan is skilled in war — do not contend with him in the field; wait until I arrive.

sentences.zh: 若能禽此人，則江東吾有也。

translations.literal: If you can capture this man, then east of the Yangtze will be mine.
translations.idiomatic: If you can capture this man, the lands east of the Yangtze will be mine.

sentences.zh: 」以功封建陽縣男。

translations.literal: " For merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: "For merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 尋為司州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he became Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 有沙門自稱僧惲，謂帝曰：「君項有伏龍，非人臣也。

translations.literal: A monk calling himself Seng Yun said to the Emperor, "On your neck a hidden dragon — you are no subject's form.
translations.idiomatic: A monk calling himself Seng Yun told the Emperor, "On your neck a hidden dragon — you are no subject's form.

sentences.zh: 」復求，莫知所之。

translations.literal: " He sought him again, but none knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: "Sought again, none knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 帝在州，甚有威名。

translations.literal: The Emperor in the province had great martial renown.
translations.idiomatic: In the province the Emperor enjoyed great martial renown.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人餉馬，帝不受，餉者密以馬系齋柱而去。

translations.literal: Once someone presented a horse; the Emperor did not accept. The giver secretly tied the horse to a hall pillar and left.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone presented a horse; the Emperor refused. The giver secretly tied the horse to a hall pillar and left.

sentences.zh: 帝出見馬，答書殷勤，縛之馬首，令人驅出城外，馬自還。

translations.literal: The Emperor came out, saw the horse, and replied with a courteous letter, tied it to the horse's head, and had a man drive it outside the city; the horse returned on its own.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came out, saw the horse, wrote a courteous reply, tied it to the horse's head, and had a man drive it outside the city — whereupon the horse returned on its own.

sentences.zh: 還都為太子中庶子，領四廂直。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he became Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, commanding the four side guards.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital he became Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, commanding the four side guards.

sentences.zh: 出鎮石頭。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to garrison Shitou.

sentences.zh: 齊明性猜忌，帝避時嫌，解遣部曲，常乘折角小牛車。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was by nature suspicious; the Emperor avoided the suspicion of the times, dismissed his personal troops, and often rode a small ox-cart with broken corners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was suspicious by nature; the Emperor avoided the suspicion of the times, dismissed his personal troops, and often rode a small ox-cart with broken corners.

sentences.zh: 齊明每稱帝清儉，勖勵朝臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming often praised the Emperor's frugality and used him to exhort court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming often praised the Emperor's frugality and held him up to exhort court ministers.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏孝文帝自率大眾逼雍州，刺史曹武度沔守樊城，武舊齊武腹心，齊明忌之，欲使後弟劉暄為雍州，暄不願出外，因江祏得留。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei personally led a great host to press Yong Province; Governor Cao Wu crossed the Han to hold Fancheng. Wu had been a trusted confidant of Emperor Wu of Qi; Emperor Ming envied him and wished to make Liu Xuan, the Empress's younger brother, Governor of Yong — Xuan did not wish to go abroad, and through Jiang Shi obtained leave to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei personally led a great host against Yong Province; Governor Cao Wu crossed the Han to hold Fancheng. Wu had been a trusted confidant of Emperor Wu of Qi; Emperor Ming envied him and wished to make the Empress's younger brother Liu Xuan Governor of Yong — but Xuan did not wish to go abroad and, through Jiang Shi, obtained leave to remain.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝擬帝雍州，受密旨出頓，聲為軍事發遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming planned to send the Emperor to Yong Province; receiving secret orders he went out to encamp, ostensibly for military dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming planned to send the Emperor to Yong Province; receiving secret orders he went out to encamp, ostensibly for military dispatch.

sentences.zh: 又命五兵尚書崔慧景、征南將軍陳顯達相續援襄陽。

translations.literal: He also ordered Minister of the Five Arms Cui Huijing and General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda to aid Xiangyang in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Minister of the Five Arms Cui Huijing and General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda to aid Xiangyang in succession.

sentences.zh: 慧景與帝進行鄧城，魏孝文帥十餘萬騎奄至，慧景引退，帝止之，不從，於是大敗。

translations.literal: Huijing and the Emperor advanced to Deng City; Emperor Xiaowen with over a hundred thousand horsemen suddenly arrived. Huijing withdrew; the Emperor stopped him but he would not obey — and there was a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing and the Emperor advanced to Deng City; Emperor Xiaowen with over a hundred thousand horsemen suddenly arrived. Huijing withdrew; the Emperor stopped him but he would not obey — and there was a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝帥眾拒戰，獨得全軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the troops to resist; he alone preserved the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the troops to resist and alone preserved the whole army.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍退，以帝為輔國將軍，監雍州事。

translations.literal: When the Wei army withdrew, the Emperor was made General Who Assists the State and overseer of Yong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army withdrew, the Emperor was made General Who Assists the State and overseer of Yong Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，雍州相傳樊城有王氣，至是謠言更甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Yong Province it was handed down that Fancheng had kingly qi; by this time the rumor grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yong Province handed down that Fancheng possessed kingly qi; by this time the rumor grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 及齊明崩，遺詔以帝為都督、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, the testamentary edict made the Emperor Area Commander and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, the testamentary edict made the Emperor Area Commander and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 時揚州刺史始安王遙光、尚書令徐孝嗣、右僕射江祏、右將軍蕭坦之、侍中江祀、衛尉劉暄更直內省，分日帖敕，世所謂「六貴」。

translations.literal: At that time Governor of Yang Province Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang, Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Director Jiang Shi, Right General Xiao Tanzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si, and Commandant of the Guards Liu Xuan took turns in the inner palace by day, each day posting edicts — what the age called the "Six Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor of Yang Province Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang, Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Director Jiang Shi, Right General Xiao Tanzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si, and Commandant of the Guards Liu Xuan took turns in the inner palace, each day posting edicts — what the age called the Six Nobles.

sentences.zh: 又有禦刀茹法珍、梅蟲兒、豐勇之等八人，號為「八要」，及舍人王咺之等四十餘人，皆口擅王言，權行國憲。

translations.literal: There were also the Imperial Blade-bearers Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Feng Yongzhi, and eight others called the "Eight Keys," and Palace Attendant Wang Xuanzhi and over forty others — all speaking the king's words by mouth and exercising the state's laws by power.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Imperial Blade-bearers Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Feng Yongzhi, and eight others called the Eight Keys, and Palace Attendant Wang Xuanzhi and over forty others — all speaking the king's words and exercising the state's laws by power.

sentences.zh: 帝謂張弘策曰：「政出多門，亂其階矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Zhang Hongce, "Government issuing from many gates — disorder has its stair.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Zhang Hongce, "When government issues from many gates, disorder has its stair.

sentences.zh: 當今避禍，惟有此地，勤行仁義，可坐作西伯；

translations.literal: To avoid calamity now, there is only this place — practice benevolence and righteousness, and one may sit and become Lord of the West.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid calamity now, there is only this place — practice benevolence and righteousness, and one may sit and become Lord of the West.

sentences.zh: 但諸弟在都，恐離時患，須與益州圖之耳。

translations.literal: But my younger brothers are in the capital; I fear they will suffer when the time divides — I must plot with Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: But my younger brothers are in the capital; I fear they will suffer when the time divides — I must plot with Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 」時上長兄懿罷益州還，仍行郢州事，乃使弘策詣郢，陳計於懿，語在懿傳。

translations.literal: " At that time his eldest elder brother Yi had finished Yi Province and returned, still handling Ying Province affairs; he sent Hongce to Ying to lay out the plan to Yi — the account is in Yi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: "At that time his eldest elder brother Yi had finished Yi Province and returned, still handling Ying Province affairs; he sent Hongce to Ying to lay out the plan to Yi — the account is in Yi's biography.

sentences.zh: 言既不從，弘策還，帝乃召弟偉及憺，是歲至襄陽。

translations.literal: When the words were not followed, Hongce returned; the Emperor then summoned his younger brothers Wei and Dan — that year they reached Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the words were not followed, Hongce returned; the Emperor then summoned his younger brothers Wei and Dan — that year they reached Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 乃潛造器械，多伐竹木，沈于檀溪，密為舟裝之備。

translations.literal: He secretly made weapons, felled much bamboo and wood, sank them in Tan Creek, and secretly prepared boats.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly made weapons, felled much bamboo and wood, sank it in Tan Creek, and secretly prepared boats.

sentences.zh: 時帝所住齋常有氣，五色回轉，狀若蟠龍。

translations.literal: At that time in the hall where the Emperor dwelt there was often vapor, five-colored and turning, shaped like a coiled dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall where the Emperor dwelt there was often vapor — five-colored, turning, shaped like a coiled dragon.

sentences.zh: 季秋出九日台，忽暴風起，煙塵四合，帝所居獨白日清朗，其上紫雲騰起，形如傘蓋，望者莫不異焉。

translations.literal: In late autumn he went out to the Double-Ninth Platform; suddenly a violent wind rose, dust and smoke joining on four sides — only where the Emperor dwelt was clear daylight; above it purple clouds rose, shaped like a canopy; all who saw were struck.
translations.idiomatic: In late autumn he went out to the Double-Ninth Platform; suddenly a violent wind rose and dust joined on four sides — only where the Emperor dwelt was clear daylight; above it purple clouds rose shaped like a canopy, and all who saw were struck.

sentences.zh: 尋而大臣相次誅戮。

translations.literal: Soon after, great ministers were executed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, great ministers were executed one after another.

sentences.zh: 永元二年冬，懿又被害。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Yongyuan, Yi was again killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yongyuan, Yi was again killed.

sentences.zh: 信至，帝密召長史王茂、中兵呂僧珍、別駕柳慶遠、功曹史起士瞻等謀之。

translations.literal: When the letter arrived, the Emperor secretly summoned Chief Administrator Wang Mao, Central Army Lü Sengzhen, Vice Director Liu Qingyuan, Merit Officer Shi Qishi, and others to plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter arrived, the Emperor secretly summoned Chief Administrator Wang Mao, Central Army Lü Sengzhen, Vice Director Liu Qingyuan, Merit Officer Shi Qishi, and others to plot.

sentences.zh: 既定，以十一月乙巳召僚佐集於聽事，告以舉兵。

translations.literal: When settled, on yisi of the eleventh month he summoned staff to assemble in the audience hall and announced raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was settled, on yisi of the eleventh month he summoned staff to the audience hall and announced raising troops.

sentences.zh: 是日建牙，出檀溪竹木裝舸艦，旬日大辦。

translations.literal: That day he raised the army standard, brought out the bamboo and wood from Tan Creek to fit out boats and warships; in ten days all was ready.
translations.idiomatic: That day he raised the army standard and brought out Tan Creek's bamboo and wood to fit out boats and warships; in ten days all was ready.

sentences.zh: 百姓願從者，得鐵馬五千匹，甲士三萬人。

translations.literal: Common people who wished to follow obtained five thousand iron horses and thirty thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Common people who wished to follow provided five thousand iron horses and thirty thousand armored soldiers.

sentences.zh: 先是，東昏以劉山陽為巴西太守，使過荊州就行事蕭穎胄以襲襄陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Donghun had made Liu Shanyang Administrator of Brazil and sent him through Jing Province to have Acting Governor Xiao Yingzhao strike Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Donghun had made Liu Shanyang Administrator of Brazil and sent him through Jing Province to have Acting Governor Xiao Yingzhao strike Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 帝知其謀，乃遣參軍王天武、龐慶國詣江陵，遍與州府人書論軍事。

translations.literal: Knowing their plot, the Emperor sent Staff Officer Wang Tianwu and Pang Qingguo to Jiangling, writing widely to men of the province and prefecture on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their plot, the Emperor sent Staff Officer Wang Tianwu and Pang Qingguo to Jiangling, writing widely to men of the province and prefecture on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天武既發，帝謂諮議參軍張弘策曰：「今日天武坐收天下矣。

translations.literal: After Tianwu had departed, the Emperor said to Adviser Zhang Hongce, "Today Tianwu by sitting will take the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianwu departed, the Emperor told Adviser Zhang Hongce, "Today Tianwu by sitting will take the realm.

sentences.zh: 荊州得天武至，必回遑無計，若不見同，取之如拾地芥耳。

translations.literal: When Jing Province receives Tianwu, it will surely waver without plan; if it does not secretly agree, taking it will be like picking up a mustard leaf.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Province receives Tianwu, it will surely waver without plan; if it does not secretly agree, taking it will be like picking up a mustard leaf.

sentences.zh: 斷三峽，據巴、蜀，分兵定湘中，便全有上流。

translations.literal: Cut the Three Gorges, hold Ba and Shu, divide troops to settle Xiangzhong — and the upper reaches will be wholly held.
translations.idiomatic: Cut the Three Gorges, hold Ba and Shu, divide troops to settle Xiangzhong — and the upper reaches will be wholly held.

sentences.zh: 以此威聲，臨九派，斷彭蠡，傳檄江南，風之靡草，不足比也，政小引日月耳。

translations.literal: With this martial renown, press the Nine Branches, cut off Poyang, proclaim by dispatch to Jiangnan — wind bending grass cannot compare; it is only a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: With this martial renown, press the Nine Branches, cut off Poyang, proclaim by dispatch to Jiangnan — wind bending grass cannot compare; it is only a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 江陵本憚襄陽人，加唇亡齒寒，必不孤立，寧得不闇見同邪。

translations.literal: Jiangling originally feared men of Xiangyang; add lips gone, teeth cold — it will surely not stand alone. How can it not secretly agree?
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling originally feared men of Xiangyang; add lips gone, teeth cold — it will surely not stand alone. How can it not secretly agree?

sentences.zh: 挾荊、雍之兵，掃定東夏，韓、白重出，不能為計，況以無算之昏主，役禦刀應敕之徒哉。

translations.literal: Wielding the armies of Jing and Yong, sweep and settle the eastern Xia — even if Han Xin and Bai Qi returned, they could not reckon it; how much less an uncounted benighted lord and blade-bearers who answer edicts!
translations.idiomatic: Wielding the armies of Jing and Yong, sweep and settle the eastern Xia — even if Han Xin and Bai Qi returned, they could not reckon it; how much less an uncounted benighted lord and blade-bearers who answer edicts!

sentences.zh: 」及山陽至巴陵，帝復令天武齎書與穎胄兄弟。

translations.literal: " When Shanyang reached Baling, the Emperor again had Tianwu carry letters to the Yingzhao brothers.
translations.idiomatic: "When Shanyang reached Baling, the Emperor again had Tianwu carry letters to the Yingzhao brothers.

sentences.zh: 去後，帝謂張弘策曰：「用兵之道，攻心為上，攻城次之；

translations.literal: After he left, the Emperor said to Zhang Hongce, "The way of using troops — attack the heart first, attack the city second.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, the Emperor told Zhang Hongce, "The way of using troops — attack the heart first, attack the city second.

sentences.zh: 心戰為上，兵戰次之，今日是也。

translations.literal: Heart-battle first, weapon-battle second — today is such a day.
translations.idiomatic: Heart-battle first, weapon-battle second — today is such a day.

sentences.zh: 近遣天武往州府，人皆有書，今段止有兩封，與行事兄弟，雲'一二天武口具'。

translations.literal: Recently I sent Tianwu to the province and prefecture — all had letters; this time there are only two, to the acting governor's brothers, saying 'one-two Tianwu will tell in person.'
translations.idiomatic: Recently I sent Tianwu to the province and prefecture — all had letters; this time there are only two, to the acting governor's brothers, saying 'one-two Tianwu will tell in person.'

sentences.zh: 及問天武，口無所說。

translations.literal: When asked, Tianwu will say nothing by mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When asked, Tianwu will say nothing by mouth.

sentences.zh: 天武是行事心膂，彼聞必謂行事與天武共隱其事，則人人生疑。

translations.literal: Tianwu is the acting governor's heart and backbone; hearing this they will surely think the acting governor and Tianwu together hide the affair — then every man will grow suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Tianwu is the acting governor's heart and backbone; hearing this they will surely think the acting governor and Tianwu together hide the affair — then every man will grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 山陽惑於眾口，判相嫌貳，則行事進退無以自明，是馳兩空函定一州矣。

translations.literal: Shanyang, confused by many mouths, will judge mutual suspicion; then the acting governor, advance or retreat, cannot clarify himself — it is driving two empty letters to settle a province.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang, confused by many mouths, will judge mutual suspicion; then the acting governor, advance or retreat, cannot clarify himself — it is driving two empty letters to settle a province.

sentences.zh: 」山陽至江安，聞之，果疑不上。

translations.literal: " Shanyang reached Jiang'an, heard of it, and indeed suspected and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: "Shanyang reached Jiang'an, heard of it, and indeed suspected and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 柳忱勸斬天武，送首山陽，穎胄乃謂天武曰：「天下之事，縣之在卿，今就卿借頭，以詐山陽；

translations.literal: Liu Chen urged beheading Tianwu and sending the head to Shanyang; Yingzhao then said to Tianwu, "Affairs of the realm hang on you; now I borrow your head to deceive Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chen urged beheading Tianwu and sending the head to Shanyang; Yingzhao then said to Tianwu, "Affairs of the realm hang on you; now I borrow your head to deceive Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 昔樊於期亦以頭借荊軻。

translations.literal: Formerly Fan Yuqi also lent his head to Jing Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Fan Yuqi also lent his head to Jing Ke.

sentences.zh: 」於是斬之，送首山陽，山陽信之，馳入城，將踰閾，縣門發，折其車轅，投車而走，中兵參軍陳秀拔戟逐之，斬於門外，傳首於帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they beheaded him and sent the head to Shanyang; Shanyang believed it, galloped into the city, and as he was about to cross the threshold the county gate sprang — breaking his carriage shaft, he cast aside the carriage and fled; Central Army Officer Chen Xiu pursued with halberd and beheaded him outside the gate; the head was sent to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: "Thereupon they beheaded him and sent the head to Shanyang; Shanyang believed it, galloped into the city, and as he was about to cross the threshold the county gate sprang — breaking his carriage shaft, he cast aside the carriage and fled; Central Army Officer Chen Xiu pursued with halberd and beheaded him outside the gate; the head was sent to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 仍以南康王尊號之議來告，且曰：「時有未利，當須來年二月。

translations.literal: Still they sent word of the plan to honor the Prince of Nankang, saying also, "The time is not yet favorable — we must wait until the second month of next year.
translations.idiomatic: Still they sent word of the plan to honor the Prince of Nankang, saying also, "The time is not yet favorable — we must wait until the second month of next year.

sentences.zh: 遽便進兵，恐非廟算。

translations.literal: To advance troops in haste — I fear it is not what the temple calculated.
translations.idiomatic: To advance troops in haste — I fear it is not what the temple calculated.

sentences.zh: 」帝答曰：「今坐甲十萬，糧用自竭，若頓兵十旬，必生悔吝。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied, "Now sitting with armor, a hundred thousand — provisions will exhaust themselves; if we halt ten ten-day periods, regret will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor replied, "Now sitting with armor, a hundred thousand — provisions will exhaust themselves; if we halt ten ten-day periods, regret will surely arise.

sentences.zh: 且太白出西方，仗義而動，天時人謀，有何不利？

translations.literal: Moreover the White Planet has come out in the west — acting in righteousness, heaven's time and men's counsel — what is not favorable?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the White Planet has come out in the west — acting in righteousness, heaven's time and men's counsel — what is not favorable?

sentences.zh: 昔武王伐紂，行逆太歲，復須待年月乎？

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu attacked Zhou — marching against the Grand Year, must one again wait for year and month?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly King Wu attacked Zhou — marching against the Grand Year, must one again wait for year and month?

sentences.zh: 」竟陵太守曹景宗遣杜思沖勸帝迎南康，都襄陽，待正尊號，帝不從。

translations.literal: " Governor of Jingling Cao Jingzong sent Du Sichong to urge the Emperor to welcome the Prince of Nankang, establish the capital at Xiangyang, and await the proper honorific — the Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: "Governor of Jingling Cao Jingzong sent Du Sichong to urge the Emperor to welcome the Prince of Nankang, establish the capital at Xiangyang, and await the proper honorific — the Emperor did not follow.

sentences.zh: 王茂又私于張弘策曰：「今以南康置人手中，彼挾天子以令諸侯，節下前去為人所使，此豈歲寒之計。

translations.literal: Wang Mao also privately told Zhang Hongce, "Now with the Prince of Nankang placed in another's hands, he will hold the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords — my lord going forward will be used by others; this is no plan for hard times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao also privately told Zhang Hongce, "Now with the Prince of Nankang placed in another's hands, he will hold the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords — my lord going forward will be used by others; this is no plan for hard times.

sentences.zh: 」弘策言之於帝，帝曰：「若前途大事不捷，故自蘭艾同焚；

translations.literal: " Hongce spoke to the Emperor; the Emperor said, "If the great affair ahead does not succeed, orchid and mugwort will burn together.
translations.idiomatic: "Hongce spoke to the Emperor; the Emperor said, "If the great affair ahead does not succeed, orchid and mugwort will burn together.

sentences.zh: 若功業克建，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: If the enterprise is established, who will dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: If the enterprise is established, who will dare not follow?

sentences.zh: 豈是碌碌受人處分！

translations.literal: How could I tamely accept another's disposal!
translations.idiomatic: How could I tamely accept another's disposal!

sentences.zh: 「于沔南立新野郡，以集新附。

translations.literal: " South of the Han he established Xinye Command to gather new adherents.
translations.idiomatic: "South of the Han he established Xinye Command to gather new adherents.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，南康王為相國，以帝為征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, the Prince of Nankang became Prince of the State; the Emperor was made General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, the Prince of Nankang became Prince of the State; the Emperor was made General Who Conquers the East.

sentences.zh: 戊申，帝發襄陽。

translations.literal: On wushen the Emperor departed Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Emperor departed Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 自冬積霰，至是開霽，士卒咸悅。

translations.literal: From winter snow had accumulated; by now the sky cleared — the soldiers all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: From winter snow had accumulated; by now the sky cleared — the soldiers all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 帝遂留弟偉守襄陽城，謂曰：「當置心於襄陽人腹中，推誠信之，勿有疑也。

translations.literal: The Emperor left his younger brother Wei to guard Xiangyang city, saying, "Place your heart in the bellies of the people of Xiangyang; extend trust to them — have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor left his younger brother Wei to guard Xiangyang city, saying, "Place your heart in the bellies of the people of Xiangyang; extend trust to them — have no doubts.

sentences.zh: 天下一家，乃當相見。

translations.literal: When all under heaven is one family, we shall meet again.
translations.idiomatic: When all under heaven is one family, we shall meet again.

sentences.zh: 」遂移檄建鄴，闡揚威武。

translations.literal: " He then moved a proclamation to Jianye, displaying martial might.
translations.idiomatic: "He then moved a proclamation to Jianye, displaying martial might.

sentences.zh: 及至竟陵，命長史王茂與太守曹景宗為前軍，中兵參軍張法安守竟陵城。

translations.literal: Reaching Jingling, he ordered Chief Administrator Wang Mao and Governor Cao Jingzong as vanguard, Central Army Officer Zhang Fa'an to guard Jingling city.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jingling, he ordered Chief Administrator Wang Mao and Governor Cao Jingzong as vanguard, Central Army Officer Zhang Fa'an to guard Jingling city.

sentences.zh: 茂、景宗帥眾濟岸，進頓九里。

translations.literal: Mao and Jingzong led the host across the shore and advanced to encamp at Jiuli.
translations.idiomatic: Mao and Jingzong led the host across the shore and advanced to encamp at Jiuli.

sentences.zh: 其日，郢州刺史張沖迎戰，茂等大破之。

translations.literal: That day, Governor of Ying Zhang Chong came out to battle; Mao and the others routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Governor of Ying Zhang Chong came out to battle; Mao and the others routed him greatly.

sentences.zh: 荊州遣冠軍將軍鄧元起、軍主王世興、田安等會大軍于夏口。

translations.literal: Jing Province sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi, Army Commander Wang Shixing, Tian An, and others to join the great army at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi, Army Commander Wang Shixing, Tian An, and others to join the great army at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 帝築漢口城以守魯山，命水軍主張惠紹、朱思遠等游遏中江，絕郢、魯二城信使。

translations.literal: The Emperor built Hankou city to hold Lushan, ordering naval commanders Zhang Huishao, Zhu Siyuan, and others to patrol and block the middle river, cutting messengers between Ying and Lu cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor built Hankou city to hold Lushan, ordering naval commanders Zhang Huishao, Zhu Siyuan, and others to patrol and block the middle river, cutting messengers between Ying and Lu cities.

sentences.zh: 時張沖死，其眾推軍主薛元嗣及沖長史程茂為主。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Chong had died; his host pushed Army Commander Xue Yuansi and Chong's Chief Administrator Cheng Mao as leaders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Chong had died; his host pushed Army Commander Xue Yuansi and Chong's Chief Administrator Cheng Mao as leaders.

sentences.zh: 三月乙巳，南康王即帝位於江陵。

translations.literal: On yisi of the third month, the Prince of Nankang took the throne at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi of the third month, the Prince of Nankang took the throne at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 遙廢東昏為涪陵王，以帝為尚書左僕射，加征東大將軍、都督征討諸軍，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: From afar Donghun was deposed as Prince of Fuling; the Emperor was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, additionally Great General Who Conquers the East, Area Commander of armies for suppression, with the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: From afar Donghun was deposed as Prince of Fuling; the Emperor was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, additionally Great General Who Conquers the East, Area Commander of armies for suppression, with the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 西台又遣冠軍將軍蕭穎達領兵來會。

translations.literal: The Western Platform also sent Champion General Xiao Yingda leading troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Platform also sent Champion General Xiao Yingda leading troops to join.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝出沔，命王茂、蕭穎達等逼郢城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Emperor went out on the Han; he ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and others to press Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Emperor went out on the Han; he ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and others to press Ying city.

sentences.zh: 五月己酉，帝移屯漢南。

translations.literal: On jiyou of the fifth month the Emperor moved camp to the south of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou of the fifth month the Emperor moved camp to the south of the Han.

sentences.zh: 是日，有紫雲如蓋，蔭於壘幕。

translations.literal: That day, purple clouds like a canopy shaded the tents.
translations.idiomatic: That day, purple clouds like a canopy shaded the tents.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，東昏遣甯朔將軍吳子陽、光子衿等十三軍救郢州，進據巴口。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Donghun sent Pacifier General Wu Ziyang, Guang Zijin, and thirteen armies to rescue Ying Province, advancing to hold Bakou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Donghun sent Pacifier General Wu Ziyang, Guang Zijin, and thirteen armies to rescue Ying Province, advancing to hold Bakou.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝命王茂帥軍主曹仲宗、康絢、武會超等潛師襲加湖，將逼子陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor ordered Wang Mao to lead Army Commanders Cao Zhongzong, Kang Xuan, Wu Huichao, and others with a hidden force to strike Jiahu, about to press Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor ordered Wang Mao to lead Army Commanders Cao Zhongzong, Kang Xuan, Wu Huichao, and others with a hidden force to strike Jiahu, about to press Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 水涸不通艦，子衿喜。

translations.literal: The water dried and ships could not pass; Zijin rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The water dried and ships could not pass; Zijin rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 其夜流星墜其城，四更中無雨而水暴長，眾軍乘流齊進，鼓噪攻之，俄而大潰，子陽等竄走，眾盡溺于江，王茂虜其餘而旋。

translations.literal: That night a falling star struck their city; in the fourth watch without rain the water suddenly rose — the armies rode the current forward together, drumming and shouting in attack; soon they collapsed greatly; Ziyang and the others fled; the host all drowned in the river; Wang Mao captured the remainder and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night a falling star struck their city; in the fourth watch without rain the water suddenly rose — the armies rode the current forward together, drumming and shouting in attack; soon they collapsed greatly; Ziyang and the others fled; the host all drowned in the river; Wang Mao captured the remainder and returned.

sentences.zh: 郢、魯二城相視奪氣。

translations.literal: Ying and Lu cities looked at each other and lost spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Lu cities looked at each other and lost spirit.

sentences.zh: 先是，東昏遣冠軍將軍陳伯之鎮江州，為子陽等聲援。

translations.literal: Earlier, Donghun had sent Champion General Chen Bozhi to garrison Jiang Province as vocal support for Ziyang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Donghun had sent Champion General Chen Bozhi to garrison Jiang Province as vocal support for Ziyang and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「夫征討未必須實力，所聽威聲耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the generals, "Suppression need not always use real force — what is heard is martial renown.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the generals, "Suppression need not always use real force — what is heard is martial renown.

sentences.zh: 今加湖之敗，誰不讋服。

translations.literal: Now with defeat at Jiahu, who will not submit in fear?
translations.idiomatic: Now with defeat at Jiahu, who will not submit in fear?

sentences.zh: 陳武牙即伯之之子，狼狽奔歸，彼間人情，理當兇懼。

translations.literal: Chen Wuya is Bozhi's son, fleeing in disarray home — the sentiment there should be fierce fear.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wuya is Bozhi's son, fleeing in disarray home — the sentiment there should be fierce fear.

sentences.zh: 我謂九江傳檄可定也。

translations.literal: I say Jiujiang can be settled by proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: I say Jiujiang can be settled by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 」因命搜所獲俘囚，得伯之幢主蘇隆之，厚加賞賜，使致命焉。

translations.literal: " He then ordered a search among captured prisoners and obtained Bozhi's banner-commander Su Longzhi; he richly rewarded him and sent him with a message.
translations.idiomatic: "He then ordered a search among captured prisoners and obtained Bozhi's banner-commander Su Longzhi; he richly rewarded him and sent him with a message.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魯山城主孫樂祖降。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Lushan garrison commander Sun Lezu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Lushan garrison commander Sun Lezu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己未夜，郢城有數百毛人踰堞且泣，因投黃鵠磯，蓋城之精也。

translations.literal: On the night of jiwei, in Ying city several hundred hairy men climbed the parapet weeping, then threw themselves into Huanghe Isle — probably the city's essence.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jiwei, in Ying city several hundred hairy men climbed the parapet weeping, then threw themselves into Huanghe Isle — probably the city's essence.

sentences.zh: 及旦，其城主程茂、薛元嗣遣參軍朱曉求降。

translations.literal: At dawn, garrison commanders Cheng Mao and Xue Yuansi sent Staff Officer Zhu Xiao to seek surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, garrison commanders Cheng Mao and Xue Yuansi sent Staff Officer Zhu Xiao to seek surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「城中自可不識天命，何意恒罵？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Within the city you yourselves could not know heaven's mandate — why constantly curse?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Within the city you yourselves could not know heaven's mandate — why constantly curse?

sentences.zh: 「曉曰：「明公未之思耳，桀犬何嘗不吠堯。

translations.literal: " Xiao said, "My lord has not considered — Jie's dog, did it not bark at Yao?
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao said, "My lord has not considered — Jie's dog, did it not bark at Yao?

sentences.zh: 」初，郢城之閉，將佐文武男女口十餘萬人，疾疫流腫死者十七八。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Ying city closed, civil and military men and women numbered over a hundred thousand; plague and swelling killed seven or eight in ten.
translations.idiomatic: "Earlier, when Ying city closed, civil and military men and women numbered over a hundred thousand; plague and swelling killed seven or eight in ten.

sentences.zh: 及城開，帝並加隱恤，其死者命給棺槥。

translations.literal: When the city opened, the Emperor all showed hidden kindness; for the dead he ordered coffins provided.
translations.idiomatic: When the city opened, the Emperor all showed hidden kindness; for the dead he ordered coffins provided.

sentences.zh: 東昏聞郢城沒，乃為城守計，簡二尚方二冶囚徒以配軍。

translations.literal: Donghun, hearing Ying city had fallen, then made plans for city defense, selecting convicts from the two Directorate workshops and two smelting works to assign to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun, hearing Ying city had fallen, then made plans for city defense, selecting convicts from the two Directorate workshops and two smelting works to assign to the army.

sentences.zh: 其不可活者，於朱雀門內日斬百餘人。

translations.literal: Those who could not be kept alive — at Zhuque Gate within, over a hundred were beheaded daily.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not be kept alive — at Zhuque Gate within, over a hundred were beheaded daily.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王亮苦諫，不從。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang remonstrated bitterly; he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang remonstrated bitterly; he did not follow.

sentences.zh: 陳伯之遣蘇隆之反命，求未便進軍。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi sent Su Longzhi back with his answer, asking that advance not yet be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi sent Su Longzhi back with his answer, asking that advance not yet be convenient.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「伯之此言，意懷首鼠，可及其猶豫逼之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Bozhi's words show a wavering heart — while he still hesitates, press him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Bozhi's words show a wavering heart — while he still hesitates, press him.

sentences.zh: 」乃命鄧元起即日沿流。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Deng Yuanqi that same day along the current.
translations.idiomatic: "He then ordered Deng Yuanqi that same day along the current.

sentences.zh: 八月，天子遣兼黃門郎蘇回勞軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Son of Heaven sent Concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Su Hui to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Son of Heaven sent Concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Su Hui to comfort the army.

sentences.zh: 帝登舟，命諸軍以次進路，留上庸太守韋叡守郢城，行州事。

translations.literal: The Emperor boarded ship and ordered the armies to advance in order; he left Governor of Shangyong Wei Rui to guard Ying city and handle provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor boarded ship and ordered the armies to advance in order; he left Governor of Shangyong Wei Rui to guard Ying city and handle provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 鄧元起將至尋陽，陳伯之猶懼，乃收兵退保湖口，留其子武牙守盆城。

translations.literal: As Deng Yuanqi was about to reach Xunyang, Chen Bozhi still feared and gathered troops to withdraw and hold Hukou, leaving his son Wuya to guard Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: As Deng Yuanqi was about to reach Xunyang, Chen Bozhi still feared and gathered troops to withdraw and hold Hukou, leaving his son Wuya to guard Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 及帝至，乃束甲請罪。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived, he bound armor and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor arrived, he bound armor and requested punishment.

sentences.zh: 九月，天子詔帝平定東夏，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to pacify the eastern Xia, acting as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to pacify the eastern Xia, acting as convenient.

sentences.zh: 前軍之次蕪湖，南豫州刺史申胄棄姑孰走，至是大軍進據之。

translations.literal: The vanguard halted at Wuhu; Governor of Southern Yu Shen Zhou abandoned Gushu and fled — then the great army advanced and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard halted at Wuhu; Governor of Southern Yu Shen Zhou abandoned Gushu and fled — then the great army advanced and held it.

sentences.zh: 自發雍州，帝所乘艦恒有兩龍導引，左右莫不見者。

translations.literal: From departing Yong Province, the ship the Emperor rode always had two dragons guiding — those left and right all saw.
translations.idiomatic: From departing Yong Province, the ship the Emperor rode always had two dragons guiding — those left and right all saw.

sentences.zh: 緣道奉迎百姓，皆如挾纊。

translations.literal: Common people along the road came to welcome; all were as if carrying cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Common people along the road came to welcome; all were as if carrying cotton.

sentences.zh: 仍遣曹景宗、蕭穎達領馬步進頓江寧。

translations.literal: He then sent Cao Jingzong and Xiao Yingda leading horse and foot to advance and encamp at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Cao Jingzong and Xiao Yingda leading horse and foot to advance and encamp at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣征虜將軍李居士迎戰，景宗擊走之。

translations.literal: Donghun sent General Who Conquers Barbarians Li Jushi to meet in battle; Jingzong struck and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun sent General Who Conquers Barbarians Li Jushi to meet in battle; Jingzong struck and routed him.

sentences.zh: 於是王茂、鄧元起、呂僧珍進據赤鼻邏，曹景宗、陳伯之為游兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Mao, Deng Yuanqi, and Lü Sengzhen advanced to hold Chibei Luo; Cao Jingzong and Chen Bozhi served as mobile troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Mao, Deng Yuanqi, and Lü Sengzhen advanced to hold Chibei Luo; Cao Jingzong and Chen Bozhi served as mobile troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，新亭城主江道林率兵出戰，眾軍禽之於陣。

translations.literal: That day, Xinting garrison commander Jiang Daolin led troops out to battle; the armies captured him in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Xinting garrison commander Jiang Daolin led troops out to battle; the armies captured him in the formation.

sentences.zh: 大軍次新林，建康士庶傾都而至，送款或以血為書。

translations.literal: The great army halted at Xinlin; scholars and commoners of Jiankang poured from the whole city to arrive, submitting allegiance or writing in blood.
translations.idiomatic: The great army halted at Xinlin; scholars and commoners of Jiankang poured from the whole city to arrive, submitting allegiance or writing in blood.

sentences.zh: 命王茂進據越城，曹景宗據皁莢橋，鄧元起據道士墩，陳伯之據籬門。

translations.literal: He ordered Wang Mao to advance and hold Yue city, Cao Jingzong to hold Zaojia Bridge, Deng Yuanqi to hold Daoshi Mound, Chen Bozhi to hold Limen.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Mao to advance and hold Yue city, Cao Jingzong to hold Zaojia Bridge, Deng Yuanqi to hold Daoshi Mound, Chen Bozhi to hold Limen.

sentences.zh: 道林餘眾退屯航南，迫之，因復散走，退保朱雀，憑淮自固。

translations.literal: Daolin's remaining host withdrew to encamp south of the ferry; pressing them, they again scattered and fled, withdrawing to hold Zhuque, relying on the Huai to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Daolin's remaining host withdrew to encamp south of the ferry; pressing them, they again scattered and fled, withdrawing to hold Zhuque, relying on the Huai to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 時李居士猶據新亭壘，請東昏燒南岸邑屋，以開戰場。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jushi still held the Xinting fort and asked Donghun to burn south-bank houses to open the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jushi still held the Xinting fort and asked Donghun to burn south-bank houses to open the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 自大航以西，新亭以北，蕩然矣。

translations.literal: From the Great Ferry west, from Xinting north — all was swept bare.
translations.idiomatic: From the Great Ferry west, from Xinting north — all was swept bare.

sentences.zh: 十月，東昏石頭軍主朱僧勇歸降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Shitou garrison commander Zhu Sengyong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Shitou garrison commander Zhu Sengyong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 東昏又遣征虜將軍王珍國列陣于航南大路，悉配精手利器，尚十餘萬，閹人王倀子持白虎幡督諸軍。

translations.literal: Donghun again sent General Who Conquers Barbarians Wang Zhenguo to array south of the ferry on the great road, all equipped with crack marksmen and sharp weapons — still over a hundred thousand; eunuch Wang Zhenzi held the White Tiger Banner to supervise the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun again sent General Who Conquers Barbarians Wang Zhenguo to array south of the ferry on the great road, all equipped with crack marksmen and sharp weapons — still over a hundred thousand; eunuch Wang Zhenzi held the White Tiger Banner to supervise the armies.

sentences.zh: 王茂、曹景宗等掎角奔之，珍國之眾，一時土崩。

translations.literal: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and others pincered and rushed them; Zhenguo's host collapsed like earth at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and others pincered and rushed them; Zhenguo's host collapsed like earth at once.

sentences.zh: 眾軍追至宣陽門，李居士以新亭壘，徐元瑜以東府城降，石頭、白下諸軍並宵潰。

translations.literal: The armies pursued to Xuanyang Gate; Li Jushi with the Xinting fort, Xu Yuanyu with the Eastern Headquarters city surrendered; Shitou, Baixia, and all garrisons fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The armies pursued to Xuanyang Gate; Li Jushi with the Xinting fort, Xu Yuanyu with the Eastern Headquarters city surrendered; Shitou, Baixia, and all garrisons fled by night.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝鎮石頭，命眾軍圍六門。

translations.literal: On renwu the Emperor garrisoned Shitou and ordered the armies to surround the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Emperor garrisoned Shitou and ordered the armies to surround the six gates.

sentences.zh: 東昏悉焚門內，驅逼營署官府併入城，有眾二十萬。

translations.literal: Donghun burned all within the gates, driving and pressing barracks and government offices into the city — he had a host of two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun burned all within the gates, driving and pressing barracks and government offices into the city — he had a host of two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史桓和紿東昏出戰，因降。

translations.literal: Governor of Qing Province Huan He deceived Donghun into coming out to battle and thus surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Qing Province Huan He deceived Donghun into coming out to battle and thus surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先是，俗語謂密相欺變者為「和欺」。

translations.literal: Earlier, common speech called secretly deceiving and turning "He-deceive."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, common speech called secretly deceiving and turning "He-deceive."

sentences.zh: 於是蟲兒、法珍等曰：「今日敗於桓和，可謂和欺矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chong'er, Fazhen, and the others said, "Today defeated by Huan He — it can be called He-deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chong'er, Fazhen, and the others said, "Today defeated by Huan He — it can be called He-deceive.

sentences.zh: 」帝命諸軍築長圍。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered the armies to build a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor ordered the armies to build a long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 初，眾軍既逼，東昏遣軍主左僧慶鎮京口，常僧景鎮廣陵，李叔獻屯瓜步。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the armies had pressed close, Donghun sent Army Commander Zuo Sengqing to garrison Jingkou, Chang Sengjing to garrison Guangling, and Li Shuxian to encamp at Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the armies had pressed close, Donghun sent Army Commander Zuo Sengqing to garrison Jingkou, Chang Sengjing to garrison Guangling, and Li Shuxian to encamp at Guabu.

sentences.zh: 及申胄自姑孰奔歸，又使屯破墩，以為東北聲援。

translations.literal: When Shen Zhou returned in flight from Gushu, he also had him encamp at Podun as northeast vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Zhou returned in flight from Gushu, he also had him encamp at Podun as northeast vocal support.

sentences.zh: 至是帝遣曉喻，並降。

translations.literal: By now the Emperor sent enlightened persuasion — all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By now the Emperor sent enlightened persuasion — all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣弟輔國將軍秀鎮京口，輔國將軍恢屯破墩，從弟甯朔將軍景鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent his younger brother General Who Assists the State Xiu to garrison Jingkou, General Who Assists the State Hui to encamp at Podun, and younger cousin Pacifier General Jing to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent his younger brother General Who Assists the State Xiu to garrison Jingkou, General Who Assists the State Hui to encamp at Podun, and younger cousin Pacifier General Jing to garrison Guangling.

sentences.zh: 吳郡太守蔡夤棄郡赴降。

translations.literal: Governor of Wu Commandery Cai Yin abandoned the commandery and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Wu Commandery Cai Yin abandoned the commandery and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，兼衛尉張稷、北徐州刺史王珍國斬東昏，其夜以黃油裹首送軍。

translations.literal: On bingyin of the twelfth month, Concurrent Commandant of the Guards Zhang Ji and Governor of Northern Xu Wang Zhenguo beheaded Donghun; that night they wrapped the head in yellow oil and sent it to the army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin of the twelfth month, Concurrent Commandant of the Guards Zhang Ji and Governor of Northern Xu Wang Zhenguo beheaded Donghun; that night they wrapped the head in yellow oil and sent it to the army.

sentences.zh: 帝命呂僧珍、張彌勒兵封府庫及圖籍。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Lü Sengzhen and Zhang Mile to seal the treasuries and archives with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Lü Sengzhen and Zhang Mile to seal the treasuries and archives with troops.

sentences.zh: 帝乃入，收嬖妾潘妃誅之，及凶党王咺之以下四十八人屬吏，以宮女二千人，分賚將士。

translations.literal: The Emperor then entered, seized the favorite concubine Consort Pan and executed her, and the evil faction Wang Xuanzhi and forty-eight others below were handed to the law; two thousand palace women were divided and bestowed on officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then entered, seized the favorite concubine Consort Pan and executed her, and the evil faction Wang Xuanzhi and forty-eight others below were handed to the law; two thousand palace women were divided and bestowed on officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 宣德皇后令追廢涪陵王為東昏侯，授帝中書監、大司馬、錄尚書、驃騎大將軍、都督、揚州刺史，封建安郡公，食邑萬戶，給班劍四十人，黃鉞、侍中、征討諸軍事並如故。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuande ordered the deposed Prince of Fuling posthumously changed to Marquess of Donghun, and conferred on the Emperor Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander, Governor of Yang Province, Duke of Jian'an Commandery with ten thousand households, forty ceremonial sword-bearers, yellow battle-axe, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and suppression of armies — all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuande ordered the deposed Prince of Fuling posthumously changed to Marquess of Donghun, and conferred on the Emperor Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander, Governor of Yang Province, Duke of Jian'an Commandery with ten thousand households, forty ceremonial sword-bearers, yellow battle-axe, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and suppression of armies — all as before.

sentences.zh: 依晉武陵王遵承制故事，百僚致敬。

translations.literal: Following the precedent of Prince Zun of Wuling of Jin assuming regency, the hundred officials paid homage.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of Prince Zun of Wuling of Jin assuming regency, the hundred officials paid homage.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝入屯閱武堂，下令大赦。

translations.literal: On jimao the Emperor entered and encamped at the Review Troops Hall and issued a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Emperor entered and encamped at the Review Troops Hall and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，入鎮殿內。

translations.literal: On bingxu he entered and garrisoned within the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he entered and garrisoned within the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 是日，鳳皇集建鄴。

translations.literal: That day, phoenixes gathered at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: That day, phoenixes gathered at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 又下令：「凡昏制謬賦、淫刑濫役，外可詳檢前源，悉皆除蕩。

translations.literal: He also ordered, "All benighted regulations, erroneous levies, excessive punishments, and abusive corvée — outside, examine carefully the original sources and entirely abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered, "All benighted regulations, erroneous levies, excessive punishments, and abusive corvée — examine carefully the original sources and entirely abolish them.

sentences.zh: 其主守散失，諸所損耗，精立科條，咸從原例。

translations.literal: Where chief and guard lost or scattered, and all losses occurred — establish precise statutes, all following original precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Where chiefs and guards lost or scattered goods and losses occurred — establish precise statutes, all following original precedent.

sentences.zh: 」丁亥，遣豫州刺史李元履以兵五千慰勞東方十二郡。

translations.literal: " On dinghai he sent Governor of Yu Li Yuanlu with five thousand troops to comfort the twelve eastern commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: "On dinghai he sent Governor of Yu Li Yuanlu with five thousand troops to comfort the twelve eastern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 二年正月辛卯，下令：「通檢尚書眾曹東昏時諸諍訟失理及主者淹停不時施行者，精加訊辯，依事議奏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on xinmao, he ordered, "Comprehensively inspect all bureaus of the Masters of Writing — all remonstrance litigation from Donghun's time that was unjust, and chief officials who delayed and did not implement in timely fashion — examine closely and debate, reporting according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, on xinmao, he ordered, "Comprehensively inspect all bureaus of the Masters of Writing — all remonstrance litigation from Donghun's time that was unjust, and chief officials who delayed and did not implement in timely fashion — examine closely and debate, reporting according to the matter.

sentences.zh: 其義師臨陣致命，疾病死亡者，並加葬斂，收恤遺孤。

translations.literal: Those of the righteous army who died facing the battle line, or from illness — all add burial rites and gather and comfort orphaned survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the righteous army who died facing the battle line, or from illness — all add burial rites and gather and comfort orphaned survivors.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，天子遣兼侍中席闡文、兼黃門侍郎樂法才慰勞都下。

translations.literal: " On jiawu the Son of Heaven sent Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary Xi Chawen and Concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yue Facai to comfort the capital.
translations.idiomatic: "On jiawu the Son of Heaven sent Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary Xi Chawen and Concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yue Facai to comfort the capital.

sentences.zh: 追贈皇祖散騎常侍、左光祿大夫，皇考侍中、丞相。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored the Imperial Grandfather as Regular Mounted Attendant, Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall; the Imperial Father as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored the Imperial Grandfather as Regular Mounted Attendant, Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall; the Imperial Father as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 乙未，下令：「朱雀之捷，逆徒送死者，特許家人殯葬；

translations.literal: On yiwei he ordered, "At the Zhuque victory, rebel dead sent back — specially permit family burial.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he ordered, "At the Zhuque victory, rebel dead sent back — specially permit family burial.

sentences.zh: 若無親屬，或有貧苦，二縣長尉即為埋掩。

translations.literal: If there are no kin, or if poor and bitter, the two county magistrates and commandants at once bury and cover.
translations.idiomatic: If there are no kin, or if poor and bitter, the two county magistrates and commandants at once bury and cover.

sentences.zh: 建康城內不達天命，自取淪滅，亦同此科。

translations.literal: Within Jiankang city those who did not reach heaven's mandate and brought ruin on themselves — the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Within Jiankang city those who did not reach heaven's mandate and brought ruin on themselves — the same rule.

sentences.zh: 」又下令減損浮費，自非奉粢盛，修紱冕，習禮樂之容，繕甲兵之備，此外一皆禁絕。

translations.literal: " He also ordered reduction of floating expenses — except for offering grain, repairing robes and caps, practicing ritual and music's forms, and repairing armor and weapons' equipment, beyond this all forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: "He also ordered reduction of floating expenses — except for offering grain, repairing robes and caps, practicing ritual and music, and repairing armor and weapons, beyond this all forbidden and cut off.

sentences.zh: 禦府中署，量宜罷省，命外詳為條格。

translations.literal: Imperial workshops and inner offices — according to measure abolish and reduce; order outside to detail statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial workshops and inner offices — according to measure abolish and reduce; order outside to detail statutes.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，宣德皇后臨朝，入居內殿，拜帝大司馬，解承制，百僚致敬如前。

translations.literal: On wuxu Empress Dowager Xuande held court, entered and dwelt in the inner hall, invested the Emperor as Grand Marshal, released assumption of regency — the hundred officials paid homage as before.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Empress Dowager Xuande held court, entered and dwelt in the inner hall, invested the Emperor as Grand Marshal, released assumption of regency — the hundred officials paid homage as before.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔進帝都督中外諸軍事，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前後部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，並依舊辟士，餘並如故。

translations.literal: On renyin an edict advanced the Emperor to Area Commander of all armies within and without, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court entry, no naming in congratulatory bow, adding front and rear feather-canopies and drum-and-pipe — left and right Chief Administrators, Marshals, Attendant Gentlemen, Assistants, and Clerks each four, all according to old practice recruiting gentlemen — the rest all as before.
